tokens.name: page-bg
tokens.usage: Page ground, as rendered behind the page's content. Every text pairing below is checked against it.

tokens.name: page-text
tokens.usage: Default body text on `page-bg`: the colour most of the page's text uses that reads on it (12.3:1).

tokens.name: page-surface
tokens.usage: Surface most of the page's running text sits on (cards, panels).

tokens.name: navy-900
tokens.usage: Deep trust, established authority, tradition.

tokens.name: navy-800
tokens.usage: Institutional gravitas, professional excellence. Used as text on `.logo`, `.nav a.active`, `.page-title`. 11.7:1 on `page-bg`.

tokens.name: navy-700
tokens.usage: Approachable authority, active engagement.

tokens.name: camel-100
tokens.usage: Natural luxury, soft warmth, paper texture.

tokens.name: camel-200
tokens.usage: Cream cashmere, inherited comfort.

tokens.name: camel-300
tokens.usage: Subtle borders, refined separation. Used as text on `.footer`. 1.4:1 on `page-bg` — under 3:1 here, as in the source: use it only on the lighter or darker fills the reference page pairs it with, never as text on `page-bg`.

tokens.name: camel-500
tokens.usage: Aged leather, established quality.

tokens.name: camel-600
tokens.usage: Burnished gold, subtle wealth indicator. Used as text on `.page-subtitle`, `.stat-label`, `.card-overline`. 3.2:1 on `page-bg` — large text (24px+) or non-text marks only.

tokens.name: forest-700
tokens.usage: British racing green, country club heritage. Used as text on `.status-active`. 10.3:1 on `page-bg`.

tokens.name: forest-800
tokens.usage: Deep tradition, environmental stability.

tokens.name: cream
tokens.usage: Unbleached parchment, quiet sophistication.

tokens.name: charcoal
tokens.usage: Ink on paper, readable authority. Used as text on `body`, `.nav a`, `.card-text`. 12.3:1 on `page-bg`.

tokens.name: category-tag-bg
tokens.usage: Painted directly by the reference page: background on `.category-tag`; border on `.category-tag`; text on `.category-tag`. 1.0:1 on `page-bg` — under 3:1 here, as in the source: use it only on the lighter or darker fills the reference page pairs it with, never as text on `page-bg`.
